standard_prerequisites.name: The homothety spectrum and universal injectivity of the localisation away from the zerodivisors of the fibre
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter flat.tex, labels lemma-homothety-spectrum and lemma-invert-universally-injective (proof lines 4331-4332); Algebra, definition algebra-definition-ord for the order used later
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the semi-locality statement and the universal injectivity of the map localising away from the elements that are not zerodivisors on the fibre, whose conclusions the proof uses.

core_obligations: Apply the cited lemmas to get the semi-locality of the localised ring and the universal injectivity of the map localising away from the multiplicative set of elements that are not zerodivisors on the fibre (proof lines 4329-4336).
Transport associated primes: since that map is universally injective over the base, a prime which is associated to the fibre remains associated after the localisation (proof lines 4336-4339).

Conclude: such a prime corresponds to a prime of the localised ring, hence is contained in a prime corresponding to an associated prime of the fibre, and therefore does not generate the unit ideal together with the extended maximal ideal (proof lines 4339-4342).
proof_roadmap: Transport associatedness across the localisation (proof lines 4336-4339).
Compare with the associated primes of the fibre (proof lines 4339-4342).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a module projective over a local ring whose fibre is a finite module over a Noetherian ring, no associated prime of the fibre generates the unit ideal together with the extended maximal ideal (statement lines 4314-4327, tag 05JD-adjacent). The proof uses the semi-locality and universal injectivity conclusions to see that a prime associated to the fibre remains associated after localising away from the zerodivisors of the fibre, hence corresponds to a prime of the localised ring, and is contained in a prime corresponding to an associated prime of the fibre. The transport of associatedness is the substance, so the claim is H2.
